title: A new idempotency key is made on every click, so a retry after an unconfirmed or half-failed refund can pay twice
evidence: Driven in Chromium with a routed API. api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeat of the same attempt, but refundSelected builds a fresh UUID for every click. After a refund that returned 200 and a reload that failed, the selection stayed checked and the button stayed enabled (state.selected is cleared only inside a successful load, app.js:98). A second click sent a different Idempotency-Key. Three clicks on the same order sent keys de8e1b59..., 431fe78a..., 59c556c2....
failing_case: Select one order and click Refund. The server refunds it and answers 200, but the follow-up GET /orders fails (network blip). The page shows 'Orders could not be loaded', still lists the order as selected, and the Refund button is enabled. The user clicks Refund again and confirms. A new key is sent, so the server's idempotency cannot recognise it, and the customer is refunded twice. The same happens when the first POST times out after the server processed it: the error text only asks the user to check statuses, and the button is not blocked.
remediation: Keep one key per selection and reuse it until the server gives a definite answer. Clear state.selected as soon as the refund is confirmed, before the reload. After an unconfirmed failure, keep the same key for the retry.

title: Orders that are already refunded (or pending) can be selected and sent to Refund
evidence: Driven: with the status filter set to 'refunded', the first row's checkbox could be checked and the Refund button became enabled. renderRow gives every row a checkbox. The confirm dialog then says 'This sends money back to the customers.' domain.js has no refund-eligibility rule. The server may reject the request, but the UI never tells the user why, and the confirm total counts orders that cannot be refunded.
failing_case: Filter to 'refunded', tick two rows, click Refund, confirm 'Refund 2 orders totalling $X'. The request is sent for orders that were already refunded. The server either errors (and the user sees a generic failure) or, if it is lenient, refunds again.
remediation: Add a pure canRefund(order) in domain.js (status === 'paid'). Disable the checkbox for other orders, and filter the selection with the same function before it is totalled and sent.

requirement.why: Refunding an order whose status is already 'refunded' has no sensible meaning; the repo does not state the eligibility rule.

title: A successful refund with an empty body (204, or 200 with no content) is reported as 'not confirmed'
evidence: Driven: the routed POST /refunds answered 204. request() throws 'The server sent a response that is not valid JSON.' and refundSelected shows 'The refund was not confirmed.' with no toast and no reload. refund() never uses the body, so only the status matters. The refund contract is not in the repo, so the empty body is the assumption.
failing_case: The server accepts the refund and answers 204 No Content, which is a common reply to a POST that returns nothing. The dashboard says the refund failed, leaves the order selected and the button enabled, and shows stale statuses. The user retries, and with the per-click key (see the idempotency finding) this refunds again.
remediation: Let request() accept an empty body (204, or Content-Length 0) and return null. Judge refund success by res.ok alone, and parse JSON only where the caller needs it.

requirement.why: The server contract for POST /api/v1/refunds is not in the payload; a bodiless success reply is an ordinary REST pattern.

title: Paging to the last (or first) page disables the focused button and drops keyboard focus to the body
evidence: Driven with the keyboard: focus on Next, Enter twice. On 'Page 3 of 3' Next became disabled and document.activeElement was BODY. The same happens for Previous on page 1. Nothing announces the page change either: #page is not in a live region.
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user tabs to Next and presses Enter until the last page. Focus is lost, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document and the user has to tab through the search box, filter, Refund button and Previous again to continue.
remediation: Before disabling the focused pager button, move focus to the other pager button or to #page. Better, use aria-disabled so the button stays focusable, and put #page in a role=status region.

requirement.why: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order and 2.1.1 Keyboard.

title: The page title sits 24 px left of the content below it on wide screens
evidence: Driven at 1360 px: h1 left edge was 130 px and the first stat card's left edge 154 px. main is 1100 px wide with 24 px padding inside the box-sizing border-box width, while the h1 is 1100 px wide with no padding.
failing_case: Open the page at any width above 1148 px. 'Orders' starts 24 px to the left of the stat cards, search box and table.
remediation: Give the h1 the same inner width as main: max-width: 1052px, or put padding: 0 24px on a 1100 px wrapper in both places.
